newsitem.title: USA: Senate Democrats block volunteer liability bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate Democrats block volunteer liability bill.

text.p: Senate Republicans failed Tuesday to break a Democratic filibuster of a bill protecting volunteers and non-profit groups from lawsuits for negligence.
Democrats say the bill was being rushed to the Senate without notice or proper consideration by committee and would protect such organizations as the Ku Klux Klan.
A Republican effort to break a filibuster failed on a virtual party line vote of 53-46, seven short of the required 60-vote majority. A second attempt will be made Wednesday.

The partisan battle came amid anger by Democrats over Republicans' refusal to confirm Alexis Herman as Labor secretary in a dispute with the White House over a planned executive order requiring federal construction contractors to have labor agreements.
Democratic Leader Tom Daschle has threatened to respond to the delay by holding up other legislation.

In a Senate speech Monday, Vermont Democrat Patrick Leahy, opposing a motion to bring up the volunteer protection bill, accused Republicans of a "partisan publicity stunt" that sought to take advantage of a volunteering summit opened in Philadelphia by President Clinton.
At the same time, he said, the Senate was failing to meet its reponsibilities to pass a federal budget and confirm Cabinet nominees and federal court judges.
Leahy said the bill should be called "the Ku Klux Klan protection act" because the Klan would be included in the definition of a volunteer organization protected by the bill.
He said the bill might also shield hospitals from legal liability involving the actions of a volunteer.

A sponsor of the bill, Republican Sen. Paul Coverdell of Georgia, said it was intended to encourage more people to serve their communities as volunteers by removing their fear of unwarranted lawsuits.

Under the legislation, no volunteer or a non-profit organization or government entity would be liable for harm caused by a volunteer's negligent acts or omissions. Coverdell said the bill was intended to protect volunteers who made "simple, honest mistakes."
